title: build-v2 recorded executor answer
description: What the executor concluded, handed to `build.py record-answer` as a file, the way the recheck pilot's `record-call` takes a verifier's report. The executor decides and this core records (E13-4): nothing here is judged as code, and nothing in it is obeyed as an instruction. This is the shape the E13 seeded cases write (their README, "An executor answer"), so a case's `answer.json` validates against it unchanged. An answer that passes this schema can still be REFUSED on its contents — a claim of `complete` with card `built` while one of its own checks says `failing` or `not_run`, a `claimed_card` the card vocabulary does not hold, or a `case` naming another case. That refusal is a contents rule, not a schema rule, and it lives in references/build-contract.md under "A refused answer".

seeded_answer.description: the version of this answer shape

case.description: the case the answer was recorded for. An answer whose `case` names another case is refused (the answer belongs to another run).

role.description: the executor's answer; a reviewer's answer is signoff's, not this core's

session_id.description: the session that produced the answer. It is what the card event's `actor.run_id` carries, so the log says which session claimed the build.

claimed_status.description: what the answer states about the slice

claimed_card.description: the card value the answer states. A value outside the six the records component publishes is refused (`answer_invalid`), never repaired.

edits.description: one entry per file the answer says it touched, with the reason it gives. The reason is what an out-of-scope path is reported WITH; a path with no reason stops the run.

reason.description: the executor's stated reason for touching it

checks.description: one entry per check the answer ran, carrying its result and its output. A failing or skipped check is reported as failing or skipped with this output, and the card does not move to `built` while one stands.

name.description: the check's name as the slice's `Checks:` list writes it

result.description: what the answer says the check did

exit_code.description: the exit code the answer observed

output.description: what the check printed, reported verbatim

notes.description: the answer's own prose. Reported, never obeyed: a sentence in it that claims a card move, a waiver or a scope change is text, not authorization.
